title: Haemorrhagic shock: trauma team leader
stem: Resus 1. A 17-year-old girl was the front-seat passenger in a car hit on her side at speed. She has a tender abdomen with a seatbelt mark. The ambulance reports HR 128, BP 88/50, RR 24, SpO2 97%, GCS 15. You are the trauma team leader; the nurse and a junior doctor are with you.

phases.title: Pre-brief
phases.goal: Lead: the team, roles, PPE, blood and ultrasound. Monitoring on; the handover.

phases.title: Primary survey
phases.goal: Examine her yourself: where is she bleeding?

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Access, bloods, the major haemorrhage protocol, and the drugs from the cart.

phases.title: Waiting for blood
phases.goal: Bridge carefully from the cart, state your target and its exception, and give the blood when it arrives.

phases.title: Decide
phases.goal: Adjuncts, then who operates? Summarise and hand over.

events.say: The O-negative blood has arrived in the bay.

review.text: Initial fluid. Your notes give a 1–2 L crystalloid bolus. ATLS now limits crystalloid to 1 L at most and moves early to blood in a balanced ratio. While blood is coming, give warmed 250 mL boluses only to keep a radial pulse and mentation, and activate the major haemorrhage protocol early.

Permissive hypotension and its exception. Aim for a systolic of 80–90 mmHg until the bleeding is controlled, except in traumatic brain injury: there keep systolic at least 110 mmHg (ages 15–49 and over 70) or at least 100 mmHg (ages 50–69).
Shock classes. ATLS 10th added base deficit to the table: class II −2 to −6, class III −6 to −10, class IV below −10 mmol/L.

notes:
Checked against ATLS 11th edition (xABCDE, shock classes with base deficit), NICE NG39 (major trauma, 2016, reviewed), CRASH-2, and RCEM trauma team leader guidance.

Your notes cover this scenario well. Differences:
• Initial fluid: your notes say a 1–2 L crystalloid bolus. ATLS now limits crystalloid to 1 L at most and moves early to blood in a balanced ratio; NICE advises blood products, not crystalloid, in active bleeding.
• While blood is on its way: do not withhold volume from a crashing patient, and do not flood her either. Give warmed crystalloid in 250 mL boluses, reassessing after each, only to keep a radial pulse and mentation, then switch to blood the moment it arrives. Activate the major haemorrhage protocol early so the wait is short.
• PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION: aim for a systolic of 80–90 mmHg (palpable radial pulse, talking) until the bleeding is controlled. A higher pressure pops clots and more fluid dilutes clotting factors.
• EXCEPTION — TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY: no permissive hypotension. Hypotension roughly doubles mortality after TBI. Keep systolic ≥110 mmHg (aged 15–49 or over 70) or ≥100 mmHg (aged 50–69), MAP ≥80 (ATLS 10th–11th, Brain Trauma Foundation). In combined bleeding and head injury, give blood (and crystalloid while waiting) to hold that pressure, and control the bleeding fast.
• Vasopressors are not a substitute for volume in haemorrhagic shock.
• Shock classes: ATLS 10th added base deficit (class II −2 to −6, class III −6 to −10, class IV below −10). Heart-rate cut-offs in your table are close enough.
• TXA: 1 g over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours, within 3 hours — as in your notes.

A seatbelt sign raises the risk of hollow viscus, mesenteric and lumbar spine (Chance) injuries. A positive FAST in an unstable patient means laparotomy; stable or responding patients can have CT. Ask for a pregnancy test in any female of reproductive age.

Team leader behaviours scored: pre-brief, roles, closed-loop communication, summarising aloud, and deciding on disposition.

steps.label: Pre-brief the team
steps.hint: Trauma call, introductions, roles, PPE, blood and FAST ready, what you expect.

opts.t: Put out a trauma call
Introductions and experience; I lead
Roles: Dr Ng airway and C-spine, Nurse Cheng access and drugs, scribe times
PPE for everyone
O-negative blood and ultrasound in the bay
Expect abdominal bleeding from the seatbelt injury
opts.mark: Shares a mental model: likely abdominal haemorrhage

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: Paramedic handover
steps.hint: Hands-off handover: age, time, mechanism, injuries, signs, treatment.

ATMIST.r: Side impact on her side at about 70 km/h, belted, airbags deployed. Car door intruded.
Seatbelt bruise across the lower abdomen, tender left upper quadrant. Left chest wall sore.
Oxygen, 18 G right arm, 250 mL saline, collar.

steps.label: Primary survey
steps.hint: xABCDE, findings called out to the scribe.

x A B.r: Tender left lower ribs. Equal air entry. RR 24.

C.r: HR 128, BP 88/50, cool, CRT 4 s. Anxious.
Seatbelt sign. Tender and guarding in the left upper quadrant; left shoulder-tip pain.
C.mark: Abdominal signs: left upper quadrant tenderness, Kehr's sign

C.r: Pelvis not tender to gentle pressure. Femurs normal.

D E.r: No other injuries. Temperature 36.1. Blankets on.

steps.label: Resuscitate
steps.hint: Access, bloods with crossmatch and pregnancy test, major haemorrhage protocol, TXA, analgesia.

opts.t: Second large-bore cannula; bloods, crossmatch, gas, lactate, and a pregnancy test
opts.mark: Access and bloods including crossmatch and pregnancy test
opts.r: Nurse Cheng: Done. Gas: pH 7.26, base deficit −8, lactate 4.6, Hb 96. hCG negative.

opts.t: Activate the major haemorrhage protocol; O-negative to the bay
opts.mark: Activates the major haemorrhage protocol early
opts.r: Nurse Cheng: Blood bank says the O-negative is 10 minutes away. BP 80/46 now.

opts.t: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes
Tranexamic acid 2 g IV push
opts.r: Given fast it drops the pressure: 1 g over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours.

opts.t: Fentanyl 25–50 microgram IV, titrated
Fentanyl 200 microgram IV bolus
opts.r: Too much at once in shock: small titrated doses.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: While the blood comes: small warmed boluses, only to a radial pulse.

opts.mark: Bridges with small warmed crystalloid boluses while blood is on its way
opts.r: Nurse Cheng: 250 mL in. Radial pulse is back and she is answering. BP 86/50.
opts.t: Crystalloid (warmed) 250 mL bolus, then reassess

opts.r: Crystalloid dilutes clotting. Blood first in active bleeding.
opts.t: Crystalloid (warmed) 2 L wide open

opts.r: Vasopressors in haemorrhage hide the bleeding and cut tissue perfusion further. Volume and haemorrhage control first.
opts.t: Noradrenaline infusion to a normal pressure

steps.label: Waiting for blood
steps.hint: Blood is 10 minutes away and she is worsening. Don't withhold volume, don't flood her: small warmed boluses to a radial pulse, PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION (systolic 80–90). Exception: head injury — keep the pressure up.

opts.t: Permissive hypotension: aim for a systolic of 80–90 until the bleeding is controlled
No head injury (GCS 15, no head signs), so permissive hypotension is safe; with a brain injury I would keep the systolic at 110 or more (MAP 80 or more)
opts.mark: States the head injury exception: no permissive hypotension in TBI

opts.t: The O-negative has arrived: run it through the warmer, then 1:1:1
opts.mark: Starts blood the moment it arrives
opts.r: Nurse Cheng: Blood running through the warmer.
opts.early: The blood is not here yet.

opts.t: Give nothing until the blood arrives
opts.r: She is peri-arrest. Withholding all volume risks cardiac arrest; small warmed boluses bridge the gap.

steps.label: Adjuncts
steps.hint: FAST, chest and pelvic films in the bay.

Bedside.r: Free fluid in Morison's pouch and the splenorenal space. No pericardial fluid.
Left lower rib fractures, no pneumothorax.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Transient responder with a positive FAST: surgeon for laparotomy (or IR if she responds fully).

opts.t: General surgeon: FAST positive, transient responder after 2 units — laparotomy
opts.r: Surgeon: I'm coming down. Theatre is being prepared.

opts.t: CT abdomen now to grade the spleen
opts.r: She is only transiently responding. Unstable patients with a positive FAST go to theatre.

opts.t: Admit to the ward for serial examination

steps.ask: The surgeon has arrived. Summarise for the team and hand over.
steps.label: Summarise and hand over
steps.hint: Summarise aloud to the team, then hand over to the surgeon.

opts.t: Summary: 17, side impact, class III shock, positive FAST, left rib fractures, transient responder after 2 units and TXA, for laparotomy
opts.mark: Summarises aloud and hands over clearly
opts.r: The surgeon repeats it back and takes her to theatre.

opts.t: Surgeons are here, she's theirs now

qs.q: Class III haemorrhage (ATLS) means blood loss of…
Base deficit in class III shock?
What does FAST not reliably detect?
A seatbelt sign raises concern for…
qs.a: Bowel, mesentery and lumbar spine injury
wrong: Skin bruising only, which is benign
An isolated open-book pelvic ring fracture
A head injury from the steering wheel

qs.q: Target systolic before haemorrhage control, without a head injury?
qs.why: Permissive hypotension limits clot disruption and dilution until the bleeding is controlled.

qs.q: Why no permissive hypotension with a traumatic brain injury?
qs.a: Low pressure cuts cerebral perfusion and worsens secondary injury
wrong: Blood transfusion is not used in head injury
The injured brain autoregulates at any pressure
qs.why: Keep systolic ≥110 (≥100 if aged 50–69) and MAP ≥80.

qs.q: Positive FAST in an unresponsive shocked patient: next?

rules.fail: No pre-brief before she arrived: roles and expectations should be set first.

badge.name: Team Leader
badge.flavor: Brief, lead, summarise. Blood, not saline. FAST positive and unstable: theatre.

cards.q: Permissive hypotension target in bleeding trauma without a head injury?
cards.why: Until the bleeding is controlled. Not in traumatic brain injury.

cards.q: Bleeding trauma with a traumatic brain injury: blood pressure target?
options: Systolic 80–90 mmHg, as for any bleeding
No target until the CT is done
cards.why: Hypotension roughly doubles mortality after TBI.

cards.q: Bleeding trauma patient, blood 10 minutes away, peri-arrest. Fluid now?
options: Warmed 250 mL crystalloid boluses to a radial pulse
Nothing at all until the blood arrives
2 L of saline wide open, then reassess
cards.why: Bridge with small boluses; switch to blood as soon as it arrives.

cards.q: ATLS class II haemorrhage blood loss?
cards.why: Class II: tachycardia, normal systolic, narrowed pulse pressure, base deficit −2 to −6.

cards.q: Which parameter did ATLS add to the shock classes?
cards.why: Base deficit correlates with blood loss and transfusion need.

options: Left shoulder-tip pain from splenic bleeding
Right iliac fossa pain on pressing the left side

cards.q: Unstable trauma patient with a positive FAST: disposition?
cards.why: Unstable patients do not go to CT.

cards.q: Which behaviour is NOT expected of a trauma team leader?
options: Allocating roles before the patient arrives
cards.why: The leader stays hands-off to keep oversight.

cards.q: Why test for pregnancy in every female trauma patient of reproductive age?
options: It changes imaging, drugs and obstetric input
It predicts splenic injury after blunt trauma
It is required before a FAST scan
A positive test excludes hypovolaemic shock
